findings.issue: Stage F's peak heap grows by about 1 KB per validation error, and the diagnostic cap does not limit it. This breaks the loader memory bound callers rely on (11 req 17: below 4x the source) and the package's own promise that a resource never stops the process ("a ruralzd reload keeps its active Revision"). Repro: probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp35r2int/probe_mem_test.go, run with `go test -count=1 -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp35r2int/overlay_mem.json -run TestProbeErrorMemory -v ./internal/config/schemaview/`. Input: a JSON Gateway whose one listener has `hostnames: [1,1,1,...]`, validated with ValidateWith(Options{MaxDiagnostics: 10}); 11 diagnostics are returned each time. n=100,000: 200,151-byte source, 83 MB peak heap (440x), 0.74 s. n=400,000: 413 MB (542x), 2.7 s. n=1,000,000: 2,000,151-byte source, 1,034 MB peak heap (542x), 8.0 s, 1.77 GB allocated. The split probe (overlay_mem2.json, TestProbeErrorMemorySplit) at 400,000 errors: the jsonschema/v6 call alone peaks at 155 MB, the full ValidateWith at 390 MB. So the package's mapping more than doubles the library's peak: it keeps a step, pathNode, textNode and interned segment text for every error position while the library's error tree is still referenced. Only MaxSourceBytes bounds a JSON document. Extrapolated: a 64 MiB JSON document needs about 33 GB and minutes in one worker; a YAML document at MaxDocumentTokens (about 500,000 elements) needs about 0.5 GB per worker, times W concurrent workers on a Node. The round-3 doc fix is incomplete: the doc says "Peak loader memory is what the hostile-input fixtures measure (OQ-configuration-model-18)", but those fixtures (11 req 17: 64 MiB + 1 byte, 20,001 resources, depth 65) all fail at stages A and B and never reach stage F. OQ-configuration-model-18 decides the nesting depth only, and no owner decision records this per-error cost.
findings.fix: Inside the package: (1) Make the mapping's memory independent of the number of errors once the cap is reached. Before memoizing a location, resolve its node and source position along the existing trie without creating new steps or interning text; when (file, line, column, code) already sorts after m.bound, skip the error, so only candidates that can be kept are memoized. (2) Release each visited cause (for example `e.Causes[i] = nil` after visiting it) so the library's error tree is freed while mapping; peak memory is then the larger of the validator tree and the mapping, not their sum. (3) Add a deterministic test that bounds mapping-retained memory, or a counter of memoized steps or interned texts, by O(cap x depth) for 1,000,000 type errors at cap 10. (4) Correct the MaxDiagnostics doc: nothing measures this cost today. File a contract request for the part the library holds (about 0.4 KB per error): extend the round-1 JSON token cap request (01 req 6: MaxDocumentTokens also for JSON documents) with these measurements; add a hostile-input fixture class to 11 req 17 (one validation error per node, at the YAML token cap and at the JSON source cap); and record the per-error bound, or the owner's acceptance of it, in OQ-configuration-model-18 or a new OQ row.

findings.where: internal/config/schemaview/mapping.go:529-532 (mapper.unknown, the namespace and status cases); 01 req 33
findings.issue: No test checks how far the two special messages reach. 01 req 33 gives special wording only to `metadata.namespace` ("Bundles have no namespace") and to a top-level `status` ("only Ruralz Control writes status"). The code limits them correctly with p.path.isField("metadata") and p.path == nil, but no test covers an unknown `namespace` or `status` field anywhere else. Two mutants run with go test -overlay both survive the full package suite: `case name == "status":` (p.path == nil check removed) and `case name == "namespace":` (isField check removed). With the status mutant, envelope("Upstream", `{"protocol": "http", "endpoints": [{"address": "a:1", "status": 1}], "status": {}}`) reports `spec.status: unknown field "status": only Ruralz Control writes status` and `spec.endpoints[address=a:1].status: ... only Ruralz Control writes status`. Both are wrong and both lose the nearest-name hint; the current code gives the plain `unknown field "status"` message. Source: spec lens.
findings.fix: Add named TestErrorMapping cases citing 01 req 33 for each place the special wording must not apply: an unknown `status` under spec, an unknown `status` inside a keyed list entry, and an unknown `namespace` under spec. Each expects the plain `unknown field` message, with the nearest hint where one exists. Show that the cases kill both mutants above, plus a third that matches `metadata` at any depth (`p.path != nil && p.path.elem.Name == "metadata"`).

findings.where: internal/config/schemaview/locate.go:112-123,311-316 (step.find / memo.step)
findings.issue: step.find compares tok in full with each of up to fewSteps children of equal length, but memo.step charges only `compared + len(tok)`, so the bytes of each equal-length child compared are never charged. memo.index's small-object scan, the sibling member of this class, charges len(k) for every equal-length name it compares, and the Options.Yield doc lists comparing one long token as a span charged with its bytes. Probe in a scratch copy: 8 sibling steps with 64 KiB tokens that differ only in the last byte; step(parent, last) charged 65,544 units while the comparisons read about 524,289 bytes, an 8x undercharge. Reachable with 8 equal-length long typed-map keys that each have an error below them. TestTextCharges "token looked up" uses a single child and TestStepIndex uses 2-byte tokens, so neither can see it. Source: code lens.
findings.fix: Have find also return the bytes it compared (len(c.tok) for each scanned child with len(c.tok) == len(tok), plus len(tok) for the map lookup), and charge that in memo.step. Add a TestTextCharges growth case with fewSteps equal-length long siblings (growth fewSteps*n) and a TestStepIndex case with long equal-length tokens.

findings.issue: Every RZ-CFG-013 warning for a credential-shaped literal prints the credential it detected through the diagnostic path whenever the credential sits in a mapping key, a set element, or a keyed-list key field. The keyWarning doc says the warning names "the detector, never the key", yet its path is the key itself. TestKeyCredentials checks only Message and Hint, so it passes anyway. The path is part of the text form (01 req 49), the JSON form, and the Node's warn log line (01 req 56 logs `path`). The warning that exists to keep credentials out therefore spreads them into CLI and CI output and into Node logs. For RZ-CFG-012 the 01 test plan already requires the literal to be absent from text, JSON and logs. Reproduction: `go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/probe2/overlay.json -run TestZZCredentialInPath -count=1 ./internal/config/subst/` (probe file /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/probe2/leak_test.go) fails with: `r.yaml:1:81 warning RZ-CFG-013 Route/r metadata.labels.AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP: credential-shaped mapping key (AWS access key ID) ...`; `r.yaml:1:121 warning RZ-CFG-013 Policy/c spec.config.allowOrigins[item=https://user:pass@example.com]: credential-shaped value (URL with a password) ...`; `r.yaml:1:125 warning RZ-CFG-013 Upstream/u spec.endpoints[address=https://user:pass@example.com].address: credential-shaped value (URL with a password) ...`. A plugin-config key `Bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz` and a JWT audience set element `AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP` leak the same way. These are the same path-construction sites as the unbounded diagnostic text finding, so the two fixes must compose.
findings.fix: Fix the whole class in subst. Give every RZ-CFG-013 credential warning (keyWarning, detect, detectRuns, headerValue via warn) a path that cannot hold the matched text. For a key warning, report at the parent object's path and keep the key's location. For a value warning, name by index (`[i]`) the warned scalar's own set element `[item=...]`, a small composite set element `[item={...}]` that holds it, and a keyed entry `[<key>=...]` whose key field is the warned scalar; config/canonical already names large set elements this way. The location stays the value position (J row 013). Add one table row per class member: a mapping key in labels, in annotations and in free content; a string set element; a composite set element; a keyed-list key field such as an endpoints address or a headers set name. Each row asserts the credential is absent from d.AppendText and from the JSON form, and each must fail on the current code. Correct the keyWarning doc and the TestKeyCredentials doc. File a contract request against 01 req 48 and J row 013 saying that no diagnostic of any stage (message or path) repeats a detected credential, because stage F diagnostics inside such an entry still print the key through the general path rule.

findings.issue: Diagnostics carry unbounded content text in their paths, identities and messages. Up to 10,001 diagnostics can each repeat one long key, keyed-entry key, string set element or resource name, so the text and JSON output grow about 10^4 times faster than the source. diag.List.Sort (01 req 50) renders Path.String() on every comparison that ties on location and code, and all RZ-CFG-010 or RZ-CFG-013 diagnostics of one scalar tie, so the sort takes minutes. config/canonical (WP-39) clips member names, keyed keys and string set elements in paths and shows clipped resource names (boundElem, shown). WP-36's own meter.go docs claim the same bounding, but WP-36 bounds only messages and composite set elements. Measured with go test -overlay probes (not in the repository): (1) subst: a Route with metadata.annotations {"<4 MiB of k>": "${U0}${U1}...${U9999}"} (source about 4.27 MB) and New(Options{Schemas}).Apply gives 10,000 RZ-CFG-010 diagnostics. Each Path holds the whole 4 MiB key, the text form sums to 41,944,038,890 bytes (9,816 times the source), and diag.List.Sort took 4m19.8s (1m30.5s with a 1 MiB key, 0.10s with a 1 KiB key). (2) overlay: a base Policy of type plugin and an overlay spec.config {"<4 MiB key>": {a0: {$patch: 1}, ..., a9999: {$patch: 1}}} give 10,000 RZ-CFG-005 diagnostics, all carrying the whole key; one text line is 4,194,496 bytes and the text form is about 41.9 GB. (3) subst, each class member reproduced with 1 MiB of text and 100 undefined variables: a Consumer spec.tags string element, a Route spec.match.headers entry name, and a Route whose metadata.name is 1 MiB. Each diagnostic's path element or Resource.Name was at least 1,048,576 bytes, and one text line was about 1,049,000 bytes. Stage C does not bound metadata.name length (01 req 16 to 18), so tree.ID.Name reaches both stages unbounded. The subst RZ-CFG-007 message is built as "no schema for " + Kind + " in apiVersion " + APIVersion, unquoted and unclipped, and its path is always apiVersion, even when the apiVersion is served and the kind is the unserved part. In overlay errorAt/report and subst report, copy the path and clip each ElemField name, ElemKeyed key and string ElemItem value to maxShown bytes with a copy (strings.Clone), as canonical.boundElem does. Build the Resource with a clipped name and kind, as canonical.resourceID/shown do, which also quotes non-graphic runes. Clip p.ID.String() in the overlay RZ-CFG-008 message. Otherwise report "kind %q is not served by apiVersion %q" at the kind position with path kind. Apply strconv.Quote(clip(...)) to both values. findings.where: internal/config/overlay/fuzz_test.go:191-199 (FuzzOverlay dropRemovals property), :232-256 (dropRemovals), :259-270 (nullTree)
findings.issue: The new metamorphic property in FuzzOverlay is false, so the fuzz target fails on valid inputs. It says that removing an overlay member whose value is a null tree over a base scalar changes neither the result nor the diagnostics. Three input classes break it. Each pair below, added as a seed in an overlay copy of fuzz_test.go and run with `go test -count=1 -run FuzzOverlay -overlay <ov.json> ./internal/config/overlay/`, failed with "a member holding nothing but removals over a base scalar changed the merge". (a) A $patch key inside the null tree. nullTree treats `{"$patch":null}` as a removal, but the merge correctly reports a misplaced directive (RZ-CFG-005, 01 req 25). Base `{"kind":"Route","spec":{"timeout":"5s"}}` with overlay `{"spec":{"timeout":{"$patch":null}}}` gives `[RZ-CFG-005 Route/x spec.timeout.$patch]` before the drop and `[]` after it. The nested form `{"spec":{"timeout":{"x":{"$patch":null}}}}` and the dispatch member `{"spec":{"type":{"$patch":null}}}` over a cors Policy fail the same way. (b) The patch annotation inside the dropped value. The path skip matches only the member `metadata.annotations["ruralz.io/patch"]` itself, not a parent that holds it. Base `{"kind":"Route","metadata":{"annotations":"x"}}` with overlay `{"metadata":{"annotations":{"ruralz.io/patch":null}}}` loses `RZ-CFG-005 unsupported ruralz.io/patch value null`. (c) A replace annotation. With ruralz.io/patch: replace, the overlay spec is kept even when it holds nothing but removals. Base `{"kind":"Route","spec":"x"}` with overlay `{"metadata":{"annotations":{"ruralz.io/patch":"replace"}},"spec":{"a":null}}` merges to `spec:{}`, but after the drop the result has no spec. In all three cases the merge follows 01 req 25 and its documented semantics; the oracle is wrong. A 300 s fuzz run did not reach these inputs, but each is a few bytes away from an existing seed, so the nightly fuzz job can hit any of them.
findings.fix: Fix all three classes in the oracle. nullTree returns false for any member keyed $patch, at any depth. dropRemovals skips any member whose subtree holds the ruralz.io/patch key (or the whole metadata.annotations path), and skips the root spec when the overlay root carries a ruralz.io/patch annotation. Add the three failing pairs above, plus the nested and spec.type variants, as FuzzOverlay seeds, so each class has a regression seed that fails without the fix.

findings.where: internal/config/overlay/merge.go:428-448 (settle trial loop, :442-447; m.a.clone(t.ov) at :444); internal/config/overlay/budget_test.go:108-111 and :168 (TestDiagnosticBudget producers)
findings.issue: settle's trial clones and normalizes the overlay value of every member whose base is a scalar, including members no dispatch rule tests. settle's own doc says the dispatch reads such a member the same whatever value the merge leaves, so this work is wasted, and the merge then normalizes the value again. It doubles the subtree's peak memory. When the stand-in changes the dispatch, the trial runs before the merge and before any diagnostic is reported, so it bypasses the diagnostic-budget stop that TestDiagnosticBudget pins ("a document with many more occurrences allocates no more"). Measurements: (1) base Policy {type: validation.json-schema, config: "x"} with overlay {type: {a: 1}, config: {20,000 members}} gives 180,405 mallocs, 49.9 MB allocated and 1252 Yield calls; the same overlay with type "cors" (no settle) gives 60,206 mallocs, 21.8 MB and 549 Yield calls, so 3 times the allocations and 2.3 times the work units. (2) A producer added to an overlay copy of budget_test.go, with base spec {type:"cors", m0..mk:"s"} and overlay spec {type:{a:1}, m0..mk:{x:{$patch:1,a:1}}}, run with `go test -run 'TestDiagnosticBudget/PROBE' -overlay ...`, printed "200829 allocations for 10050 occurrences, 321562 for 20100: the walk goes on past the budget". The existing row "misplaced $patch in values replacing base scalars" misses this because its dispatch does not change, so settle returns at `same`. The cost stays linear in the input and the clones are short-lived garbage.
findings.fix: Run the trial only for members the dispatch may read: those m.a.dispatchTested(static, t.key) reports, or the declared properties selectOf's proxy collects. Leave the rest as the base scalar while the dispatch is read. Better, replace clone plus normalize with a non-allocating read-only predicate that walks the overlay value under the member's schema with normalize's rules and stops at the first value that would remain. Pin it against normalize(clone) != nil with a differential or fuzz test. Add a test that counts mallocs or work units for an untested member (measurement 1) and fails without the change. Add the producer of measurement 2 to budgetProducers, plus a variant whose single dispatch-member value holds k misplaced $patch members.

findings.where: internal/config/overlay/removal_test.go:304-356 (TestDispatchTestsScalars); internal/config/overlay/merge.go:414-417 (settle doc)
findings.issue: settle's shortcut (if standing every overlay composite in leaves the dispatch unchanged, no mix changes it) assumes the rules are monotone, meaning a composite only makes rules fail. Inline, the same call ends the caller's goroutine. Input: Policy az-exit of type authz.cel with rule "exit && request.body.x", plus cache, cors and ratelimit; Gateway [cors, rl]; Route [az-exit, cache]; Options.Body calls runtime.Goexit for a rule containing "exit" (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-advr2-q4z/probe_goexit_test.go with overlay_goexit.json). At workers 2 and 4: no error, no diagnostics, and the chain has no az-exit; with an honest oracle the same Bundle gives RZ-CFG-038 and az-exit in onRequestBody. The authorization Policy is dropped and the Bundle accepted. Class members: selectAll (the zero selection is taken as a valid entry with Policy "" and no Phases, and takes slot ""); attachUpstreams (a Now that Goexits leaves a silently empty leg); the Route forEach (results[i] stays nil, which panics with a nil dereference at s.chains[c.Route]). Options.Body's doc does not forbid Goexit; only the unexported forEach does. Sibling stage G handles this case (defaults.go:423-427, errGoexit).
findings.fix: In pool.run, set a done flag after fn returns. In the deferred function, treat 'not done and recover() == nil' as a unit failure carrying an errGoexit value with the stack, record the stop as for a panic, and raise it again in the caller for every worker count, as stage G does. Document this on Options.Body and Options.Now. Add one test per member (Body in selectAll, Now in attachUpstreams, Now in the Route forEach), each at workers 1 and 4, each failing without the fix.

findings.where: internal/config/precedence/resolve.go:221-231 (addKeys) and 268-285 (selectAll: one 200-byte selection per attachKey)
findings.issue: Stage I allocates a full selection (unsafe.Sizeof = 200 B), a map entry and a keys slot for every distinct (name, scope) it sees, including names that resolve to no Policy. 02 req 40 says to skip those references, and stage H reports them as RZ-CFG-009. Input: 50 Routes, each listing 5,000 distinct absent Policy names (4.6 MB of YAML, one file per Route; /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-advr2-q4z/probe_absent_test.go with overlay_absent.json). The parsed tree plus the typed hub resources hold 86 MiB; selectAll adds 63 MiB live, 309 B per absent reference. At 1,000,000 references it adds 295 MiB live (472 MiB TotalAlloc). A 64 MiB source (about 4M 16-byte references) therefore costs about 1.2 GB in stage I alone, for references it ignores.
findings.fix: In addKeys, record a key only when b.Get finds a Policy resource; attachList already skips sel == nil. Keys are then at most 3 x Policies, which MaxResources bounds at 60,000. Alternatively, store missing keys as one shared sentinel instead of a per-key selection. Add a test that selectAll's TotalAlloc (or keys plus sels) does not grow with the number of absent references, at 1 and 4 workers.

findings.where: internal/config/precedence/resolve.go:489-506 (rule 2 replaces regardless of Phases) and rows.go:292-295
findings.issue: A Route Policy that runs in no Phase still replaces the Gateway Policy in its slot, and then appears nowhere in the effective table. Examples: headers with config {} or transform.request without body or list entries; registry Phase selection returns an empty set for both. Input: Gateway headers hg (slot hdr, request and response ops) and transform.request tg (slot t, body "x"); Route headers hr (slot hdr, config {}) and transform.request tr (slot t, config {}) (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-advr2-q4z/probe_zero_test.go with overlay_zero.json). Run reports no diagnostics. Rows returns only 'none none hg Gateway replaced in slot hdr by hr' and 'none none tg Gateway replaced in slot t by tr'. hr and tr have no row, and hub.Chain carries no entry for them, so render --effective names a replacing Policy it never shows. Spec 02 test 17 says an empty config gives no rows, but neither it nor req 35.2/51 says whether such a Policy takes part in slot replacement.
findings.fix: File a contract request or Open questions row for spec 02 req 35.2 and req 51, as the owner's decision. Options: (a) a Policy whose Phase set is empty does not replace (skipped like a scope-rejected entry), or (b) it replaces and Rows lists it with Phase and Leg none and reason 'slot <s>, replaces <g>', which needs the chain to carry it. Pin the chosen behavior with a test for headers and for transform.request/response.

findings.where: internal/config/precedence/work.go:40-47 (doc claim); resolve.go:89-93 (newSharedPhase), 619-625 (client bypass scan), 509-510 (removed sort)
findings.issue: The work.go doc says every input-length loop 'counts its elements at its own site, so the time between two reads of the timer stays bounded'. Three sites charge only after an uninterruptible O(n) pass, so the yield timer is never read inside it (01 req 53: every 256 nodes): newSharedPhase calls slices.IndexFunc over every entry of the Phase, then charge(siteShared, len); client scans the onRequestBody slice the same way, then charge(siteBypass, len); route calls slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(fate)) (k log k comparisons), then charge(siteRemoved, k). The number of resolvable Gateway Policies, which MaxResources caps at 20,000, bounds these passes, but each is still one stretch of up to about 20,000 elements (k log k for the sort) between two timer reads, against 256 elsewhere. For example, a Gateway of 19,000 headers Policies gives a single charge(siteShared, 19000). (Related but separate: the code-lens major on uncharged reference-name lengths falsifies the same work.go claim.)
findings.fix: Charge inside the passes: count in the IndexFunc predicates, or replace them with charged loops. Collect the fate keys in a charged loop and sort them with slices.SortFunc and a charging comparator. Add TestWorkCharged rows that require at least one timer read per yieldCheck elements inside each of these passes.

findings.where: internal/config/precedence/resolve.go:417-439 (attachUpstreams), :391-415 (attachGateway); 01 req 40; 03 req 11 and 15; WP-56 scope ('expr.Site from chains')
findings.issue: Stage I checks every Upstream list and builds a leg template for every Upstream, but exports leg Phases only through Route chains. 01 req 40 says 'one leg set per Upstream' is computed here and exported. 03 req 11 makes the chain resolver the source of each attachment's first Phase, and 03 req 15 has WP-56 compile Policy CEL once per distinct (scope, first Phase) over all scopes the Policy is attached at, and compile an unattached Policy at its first allowed scope. findings.fix: File a contract request with one of two changes: (a) export the per-Upstream leg sets and the Gateway base Phases, or a per-attachment view (Policy, scope, Phases, attaching resource), from stage I and carry it in hub.Validated (a WP-01 hub change); or (b) amend WP-56's scope so sites for attachments absent from every chain come from registry.Phases with the same expr.Compiler oracle, and amend 01 req 40, which says one leg set per Upstream is exported. findings.where: 00-architecture.md 3.1 (gating sentence) vs 01 req 51, 02 req 2 and 40; WP-38 contract request to WP-69
findings.issue: Architecture 3.1 says each stage stops the run once it produced an error diagnostic, and only F and H collect every finding of their stage first. Read that way, any RZ-CFG-009 from stage H stops the run before stage I, so RZ-CFG-018/019/020/029/038 in other Routes are not reported in the same run. That contradicts 01 req 51, which runs 009, 018, 019, 020 and the other cross-resource checks together so all such errors surface in one run, and 02 req 2 and 40: stage I skips unresolved references and continues for the other Routes so every error is reported in one run. Stage I already supports the spec behavior, because it skips missing references. The WP-69 contract request filed by WP-38 does not raise this conflict, so WP-69 may follow 3.1 literally and the skip logic would never run.
findings.fix: File a contract request on architecture 3.1 and WP-69: stages H and I run as one gate. Stage I runs whenever H's precondition holds (every file parsed, every identity valid, every resource decoded, per 01 req 51), even when H reported errors, and the run stops after stage I. Alternatively, record the owner's decision on which reading wins. Cite 02 req 40 and 01 req 51.

findings.where: internal/config/precedence/resolve.go:857-872 (clip)
findings.issue: The doc says clip 'allocates only the result', but a clipped slot costs 3 allocations ([]rune, string, concatenation): testing.AllocsPerRun reports 3 for a 1 MiB slot (probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-r2tq-k8m/probe/probe_clip_test.go via /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-r2tq-k8m/ov_clip.json). The []rune conversion also turns an invalid byte into U+FFFD only when the slot is clipped. Every message passes the result through %q, so the same authored byte renders differently by slot length: 64 code points give share slot "\xffaaa…", 65 give "�aaa…...". Stage G's clip (defaults/scalar.go:183-200) converts in both cases and stays consistent.
findings.fix: Return s[:i] + "...": range leaves i on a rune boundary and %q already escapes invalid bytes, so this is one allocation and gives the same rendering for every length. Update the doc and the TestClip row 'invalid UTF-8 in the kept prefix'. Alternatively keep the conversion in both branches, as stage G does, and correct the allocation claim.
